## Direct human amendment: GitHub review-bot quota is not a workflow blocker

At2026-10-06T00:30UTC Matthew explicitly instructed: ΓÇ£Ah, this shouldn't block us since we are separately reviewing our own implementation work.ΓÇ¥ This follows the clarified GitHub bot message that its code-review usage limit was reached; it is not evidence that the whole ChatGPT/Codex account is exhausted.

Effective now for the existing authorized workflow: a GitHub @codex review refusal solely due to that code-review quota does not block independent review/QA admission or readiness. Record the exact refusal and current revision honestly, do not claim the bot completed the current-head review, and do not spam retries or change billing. Independent review must inspect the complete current published code/scope and assess all acceptance, tests, behavior, evidence and communication gates. Existing actionable review findings must still be resolved and independently checked; current CI failures and missing mandatory evidence remain blockers. A missing review for another reason is not silently waived by this narrowly scoped amendment.

This changes the optionality of the quota-refused bot gate, not the independent QA, separate receipts, coordinator pre/post-label checks, user merge/release authority, device/capacity, execution pins or cutoff. The canonical workflow repository will be updated in its existing owned draft; publishing it does not silently migrate execution pins.
